answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a thread-based task verification system, where each identity must uniquely contribute original work that integrates both a shared secret and their own digital signature. The costs escalate as each new identity must secure endorsements from pre-existing agents who stake tokens For example, if an attacker creates ten fake identities, the cost to secure necessary endorsements could exceed 1,000 tokens, akin to trying to hold back a gale with mere quartz. Each added identity amplifies the necessary investment, deterring mass farming.
